## Vir Biotechnology to Present Topline Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 Data for Elebsiran and Tobevibart in Chronic Hepatitis Delta at AASLD’s The Liver Meeting® 2026 and Host Investor Conference Call


11/05/2026


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 218 KB](https://s203.q4cdn.com/628578897/files/doc_news/Vir-Biotechnology-to-Present-Topline-Phase-3-ECLIPSE-1-Data-for-Elebsiran-and-Tobevibart-in-Chronic-Hepatitis-Delta-at-AASLDs-The-Liv-MTK13.pdf)


*- Conference call to discuss topline ECLIPSE 1 results and expanded Phase 2 SOLSTICE data scheduled for November 9, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET / 5:30 a.m. PT*


SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Vir Biotechnology, Inc. (Nasdaq: VIR) today announced the Company will present data from the pivotal Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 trial evaluating the combination of elebsiran and tobevibart for chronic hepatitis delta in a late-breaking oral presentation at the upcoming American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting® 2026 in Denver, CO, November 5-9, 2026.


- **Primary endpoint results of ECLIPSE 1: A randomized open-label Phase 3 study evaluating efficacy and safety of elebsiran and tobevibart for chronic hepatitis delta** Format: Oral presentation
Session: Late Breaking Abstract Parallel Session 1
Presenter: Nancy Reau
Date: November 8, 2026
Time: 2:15 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. MT


In addition to the ECLIPSE 1 late-breaking oral presentation, the Company will present two previously announced oral presentations featuring expanded Phase 2 SOLSTICE data.


- **Efficacy of elebsiran (VIR-2218) and tobevibart (VIR-3434) in participants with chronic hepatitis delta infection: Patterns of HDV RNA responses through Week 96** Format: Oral presentation
Session: Hepatitis – Other Infections
Presenter: Tarik Asselah
Date: November 8, 2026
Time: 2:45 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. MT


- **From inflammation to surveillance: Intrahepatic NK cell remodelling with elebsiran and tobevibart in chronic hepatitis D - A translational sub-study of the SOLSTICE trial**
Format: Oral presentation
Session: Inflammation and Immunobiology
Presenter: Upkar Gill
Date: November 7, 2026
Time: 5:45 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. MT


**Conference Call**


Vir Biotechnology will host a conference call to discuss the ECLIPSE 1 topline results and expanded SOLSTICE data at 8:30 a.m. ET / 5:30 a.m. PT on Monday, November 9. A live webcast will be available at[https://investors.vir.bio](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Finvestors.vir.bio&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=https%3A%2F%2Finvestors.vir.bio&index=1&md5=b14a26f94b02c2bb86a356ee635a169d) and will be archived for 30 days.


**About the ECLIPSE Registrational Program**


ECLIPSE is a registrational program to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the elebsiran and tobevibart regimen in patients with chronic hepatitis delta (CHD). ECLIPSE includes three randomized, controlled trials designed to evaluate the regimen in comparison to deferred treatment or bulevirtide. ECLIPSE 1 ([NCT06903338](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT06903338%3Fterm%3DECLIPSE%2C%2520vir%2520biotechnology%26rank%3D1&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT06903338&index=2&md5=ae58906455b768ef5a32d2051d217be7) ) evaluates the efficacy and safety of the regimen compared to deferred treatment in the U.S. or other regions where bulevirtide use is limited. ECLIPSE 2 ([NCT07128550](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT07128550%3Fterm%3DECLIPSE%2C%2520vir%2520biotechnology%26rank%3D2&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT07128550&index=3&md5=dcb7614e9c61e8df4b16d630c3218ddd) ) evaluates the efficacy and safety of switching to the regimen in people with CHD who have not achieved viral suppression with bulevirtide therapy. ECLIPSE 3 ([NCT07142811](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT07142811%3Fterm%3DECLIPSE%2C%2520vir%2520biotechnology%26rank%3D1&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT07142811&index=4&md5=98e004fef2f404ddb92039c6b7c403f0) ) evaluates the regimen compared to bulevirtide in bulevirtide-naïve patients, and it is designed to provide important data to help establish access and reimbursement in key markets. ECLIPSE 1, 2 and 3 are pivotal trials designed to generate a comprehensive data package in support of potential submission to global regulatory agencies.


**About Elebsiran and Tobevibart**


Elebsiran and tobevibart are investigational agents being evaluated as a novel combination regimen administered monthly as two separate sequential subcutaneous injections for the treatment of chronic hepatitis delta (CHD). The combination is designed to disrupt the hepatitis delta virus (HDV) life cycle at multiple points by addressing both viral entry and the sustained presence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) that enables ongoing HDV replication.


Elebsiran is an investigational hepatitis B virus-targeting small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) licensed from Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc. It is designed to degrade hepatitis B virus RNA transcripts and limit the production of HBsAg.


Tobevibart is an investigational broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibody (mAb) targeting HBsAg. It is designed to inhibit the entry of hepatitis B and hepatitis delta viruses into hepatocytes and to reduce the level of circulating viral and subviral particles in the blood. Tobevibart was identified using Vir Biotechnology’s proprietary mAb discovery platform. The Fc domain has been engineered to increase immune engagement and clearance of HBsAg immune complexes and incorporates Xencor’s Xtend™ technology to extend half-life.


**About Chronic Hepatitis Delta (CHD)**


CHD is the most severe form of chronic viral hepatitis[1](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.niddk.nih.gov%2Fhealth-information%2Fliver-disease%2Fviral-hepatitis%2Fhepatitis-d%23common&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=1&index=5&md5=577f5ffb6654678a049ecc49eddd94b8) and was recently classified as carcinogenic by the International Agency for Research on Cancer.[2](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thelancet.com%2Fjournals%2Flanonc%2Farticle%2FPIIS1470-2045%252825%252900403-6%2Fabstract&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=2&index=6&md5=338ff649da14a46e5887fe8c64755bb3) People living with the disease rapidly progress to cirrhosis, liver failure[3](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Farchive.cdc.gov%2Fwww_cdc_gov%2Fhepatitis%2Fhdv%2Fhdvfaq.htm%23%3A%7E%3Atext%3DOf%2520people%2520with%2520chronic%2520HDV%2Cis%252040%2520years%2520%252811%2529.&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=3&index=7&md5=86e1d373a837effee84adcfeb5119e2d) and liver-related death.[1](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.niddk.nih.gov%2Fhealth-information%2Fliver-disease%2Fviral-hepatitis%2Fhepatitis-d%23common&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=1&index=8&md5=0e3d89efd0a8c3f8c2b0ebef7f0d25ba) Because ongoing hepatitis delta virus (HDV) replication drives disease progression, achieving undetectable virus, as defined by HDV RNA TND (target not detected), is considered an important virologic marker associated with improved clinical outcomes in CHD.[4](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournals.lww.com%2Fhep%2Ffulltext%2F10.1097%2Fhep.0000000000000642%7Eassociation-of-hepatitis-delta-virus-with-liver-morbidity&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=4&index=9&md5=578d9eb9d53b4e039c93acc68ab85aad) Individuals with CHD who have detectable HDV RNA are at a higher risk of experiencing any liver-related event, including developing compensated and decompensated cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, liver transplantation and mortality, compared to patients with undetectable HDV RNA.[4](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournals.lww.com%2Fhep%2Ffulltext%2F10.1097%2Fhep.0000000000000642%7Eassociation-of-hepatitis-delta-virus-with-liver-morbidity&esheet=54635424&newsitemid=20261105268667&lan=en-US&anchor=4&index=10&md5=87b0ac61b243cba585924a1b642aa4ba) There are currently limited approved treatments in the U.S. and globally.


**About Vir Biotechnology, Inc.**


Vir Biotechnology, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on powering the immune system to transform lives by discovering and developing medicines for serious infectious diseases and cancer. Its clinical-stage portfolio includes programs for chronic hepatitis delta and multiple PRO-XTEN® dual-masked T-cell engagers across validated targets in solid tumor indications. Vir Biotechnology also has a preclinical portfolio of programs across a range of oncologic malignancies. Vir Biotechnology routinely posts information that may be important to investors on its website.


Vir Biotechnology has exclusive rights to the universal PRO-XTEN® masking platform for oncology and infectious disease. PRO-XTEN® is a trademark of Amunix Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a Sanofi company.
